name: Opus Quality Defensive
strategy: Low-beta quality/defensive core: a trimmed healthcare anchor, the min-vol sleeve, a new consumer-staples sleeve, a small energy diversifier, the AI-exposed quality factor sleeve removed, and 32% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: The book did its job (+2.14% vs SPY -7.89%) but research shows two problems in it. First, XLV fell ~6% this week partly for a healthcare-specific reason: CMS's proposed Medicare Advantage audit/clawback rule (released 11-16, comment period to 2027-01-19) sent UNH down ~17% on the week and hit managed care broadly, with MRK -9.5% too. That risk stays open for two months, so 38% in one sector is too concentrated; I trim XLV to 30 and move the weight into XLP, which fell only about 2% from the 11-13 close in the same tape (PG and WMT were roughly flat). Second, the selloff is an AI/semiconductor unwind (Nov 5 -4.2% day, Nvidia-led losing streak, VIX ~36), and QUAL's megacap-tech weight made it the worst leg (-7.4%); a defensive mandate should not carry that exposure into this tape, so I exit it. I considered adding Treasury duration (TLT +2.6% on the week) but rejected it: the 10-year is ~5.07% with the Fed signalling a December hike, so bonds are not a reliable hedge in this regime, and cash at 4% does the job. Gross falls 70% to 68% and cash rises to 32%. I am not de-risking further at VIX 36, because selling defensives after a fall is how a defensive book locks in losses.

positions.thesis: Healthcare remains the low-beta anchor: pharma and devices earnings do not depend on the AI capex cycle that is unwinding, and XLV is now ~6% cheaper than last week. Cut from 38 to 30 because the CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal is an open regulatory overhang on managed care (UNH, ELV, CVS, HUM) until at least the January comment deadline. The 12% stop from the fresh entry caps the damage if that broadens into a sector-wide drug-pricing or policy shock.

Min-vol, diversified across sectors, is the core expression of the mandate. It fell ~5.7% from the 11-13 close against SPY's 8.6%, which is the expected downside capture of about 0.65. Kept at 16% so the book's defensive exposure does not sit only in healthcare.

New sleeve funded from the XLV trim. Staples were the most resilient sector this week: XLP is down about 2% from 11-13 against SPY's -8.6%, with PG and WMT about flat. They have no AI-capex exposure and no Medicare policy exposure, so they diversify the healthcare anchor directly. Sized at 14% so that staples plus healthcare, at 44%, is still below the old single-sector 38% plus QUAL.

A small energy diversifier that is uncorrelated with the tech unwind: it fell only 2.3% from entry while SPY fell about 8%. Integrated majors are cash-generative with high dividends. Held at 8% rather than raised, because crude is still losing its war premium (USO -14% over a month); the 12% stop exits if that turns into a demand-recession call.
